{{Short description|Logician and philosopher}}
'''Luca Incurvati''' is a [[logician]] and [[philosophy|philosopher]], currently an associate professor at the [[Institute for Logic, Language and Computation]], [[University of Amsterdam]]. Incurvati's research areas include [[set theory]], [[philosophy of mathematics]], [[philosophy of language]], and [[metaethics]]. In set theory and philosophy of maths, Incurvati has argued for the iterative conception of sets, based on a methodology he terms ''inference to the best conception''.<ref>{{cite web
 |url= https://www.cambridge.org/core/blog/2020/02/17/arguing-about-sets/
 |title=Arguing about sets
 |last=Incurvati
 |first=Luca
 |date=2020-02-17
 |website=Cambridge University
 |access-date=2020-12-09}}</ref> Incurvati is currently the principal investigator in the Amsterdam-based project ''From the Expression of Disagreement to New Foundations for Expressivist Semantics'', for which he was awarded a prestigious [[European Research Council|ERC]] Starting Grant of 1.5 million euros.<ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://www.uva.nl/en/content/news/press-releases/2017/09/erc-awards-starting-grant-to-six-uva-researchers.html?cb
 |title=ERC awards starting grant to six UvA researchers
 |date=2017
 |website=University of Amsterdam
 |access-date=2020-12-09}}</ref> This project proposes a [[inferentialism|inferentialist]] [[logical expressivism|expressivist]] treatment of disagreement, in particular arguing that the [[speech act]] of ''rejection'' is not reducible to negated [[Logical assertion|assertion]]. For a paper produced as part of this project, Incurvati and coauthor Julian Schlöder received the 2019 Marc Sanders Prize in Metaethics.<ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://marcsandersfoundation.org/metaethics/
 |title=Marc Sanders Prize in Metaethics
 |website=Marc Sanders Foundation
 |access-date=2020-12-09}}</ref>

Incurvati earned his MPhil and PhD at [[St John's College, Cambridge|St John's College]], [[University of Cambridge]], where he worked under the supervision of Michael Potter and Peter Smith.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=268852}}</ref> He was awarded the Matthew Buncombe Prize for his MPhil thesis in 2005. Before his current position in Amsterdam, he was a lecturer at Cambridge, where he served as Director of Studies at [[Fitzwilliam College|Fitzwilliam]], [[Gonville and Caius]] and [[Magdalene College|Magdalene]] colleges.
